common_name: Black Swan Tree Peony (Near-Black Rockii Tree Peony)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early to mid fall in deep, humus-rich, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun to partial afternoon shade, setting a grafted union (if present) 4-6 inches below the soil surface to encourage the scion to form its own roots.

directions: Black Swan is a Paeonia rockii-type tree peony selected for exceptionally dark, near-black maroon flowers, among the deepest coloration available in hardy tree peonies, opening from near-black buds to velvety deep burgundy-black blooms with a satin sheen. Like other rockii-type tree peonies it is derived from wild Gansu-region mountain peony stock and is notably more cold-hardy and drought-tolerant once established than the more familiar Paeonia suffruticosa hybrids, tolerating winter lows into zone 4 without dieback. Site in deep, humus-rich, sharply drained soil where the woody framework can remain undisturbed for decades, giving full sun in cooler climates and afternoon shade where summers turn hot. Avoid heavy pruning, since flower buds form on the previous year's wood; remove only dead or damaged stems after bloom.

common_name: Boundless Bright Sky Tree Peony (Sky-Blue Lavender Rockii Tree Peony)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early to mid fall in deep, humus-rich, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun to partial afternoon shade, setting a grafted union (if present) 4-6 inches below the soil surface to encourage the scion to form its own roots.

directions: Boundless Bright Sky is a Paeonia rockii-type tree peony prized for its cool violet-blue flower coloring, among the closest to true blue found in tree peonies, with large semi-double to double blooms held above deeply cut, blue-green foliage. As with other rockii-type selections bred from wild Gansu mountain peony stock, it is exceptionally cold-hardy and tends to resent hot, humid summers more than the classic Chinese and Japanese Paeonia suffruticosa hybrids, rewarding gardeners in colder zones with reliable spring bloom. Plant in a permanent site in deep, fertile, sharply drained soil in full sun where summers are mild, or with afternoon shade where summers are hot, and avoid disturbing the root zone once the shrub is established. Only light pruning of dead or damaged wood is needed, since flower buds set on the prior season's growth.

common_name: Glory of the Sun and Moon Tree Peony (Bicolor Red-and-White Rockii Tree Peony)
scientific_name: Paeonia rockii 'Glory of the Sun and Moon'

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early to mid fall in deep, humus-rich, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun to partial afternoon shade, setting a grafted union (if present) 4-6 inches below the soil surface to encourage the scion to form its own roots.

directions: Glory of the Sun and Moon is a Paeonia rockii-type tree peony bred for a striking bicolor effect, combining warm red-toned petal bases evoking the sun with pale, moonlit outer petal tones in the same enormous, ruffled bloom. It shares the rockii group's parentage from wild mountain peonies of Gansu Province in northwestern China, giving it outstanding cold hardiness and tolerance of the lean, sharply drained soils typical of its native range. Grow in deep, humus-rich soil in full sun in cooler regions, shifting to afternoon shade in hot-summer climates, and plant where the shrub's permanent woody framework will not need to be disturbed again. Limit pruning to removal of dead or damaged wood, since next spring's flowers form on the current season's mature stems.

common_name: Jade Crown Blue Belt Tree Peony (White Rockii Tree Peony with Violet Petal Flares)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early to mid fall in deep, humus-rich, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun to partial afternoon shade, setting a grafted union (if present) 4-6 inches below the soil surface to encourage the scion to form its own roots.

directions: Jade Crown Blue Belt is a Paeonia rockii-type tree peony in the classic rockii color pattern: cool jade-white petals marked at the base with a contrasting band of violet-purple, giving each enormous bloom a distinctive banded eye. This wild-derived rockii lineage, sourced from mountain peony populations of Gansu Province, is markedly more cold-hardy than most Paeonia suffruticosa hybrids and prefers lean, sharply drained soil over rich, moisture-retentive ground. Site the shrub in a permanent full-sun location (partial afternoon shade in hot climates) in deep, well-drained soil, since tree peonies resent transplanting once their woody framework is established. Prune only to remove dead or damaged wood after flowering, leaving the prior season's growth intact to carry next year's blooms.

common_name: Noblewoman Tree Peony (Refined Lavender-Purple Rockii Tree Peony)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early to mid fall in deep, humus-rich, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun to partial afternoon shade, setting a grafted union (if present) 4-6 inches below the soil surface to encourage the scion to form its own roots.

directions: Noblewoman is a Paeonia rockii-type tree peony bearing refined, silvery lavender-purple flowers with a darker maroon flare at the petal base, a color combination traditionally prized in Chinese tree peony culture as elegant and dignified. Rockii-type tree peonies descend from wild mountain peony populations of Gansu Province and are notably hardier and more drought-tolerant once established than the familiar Paeonia suffruticosa hybrids, though they can be slower to establish. Plant in deep, fertile, sharply drained soil in a permanent site, giving full sun in cooler climates and afternoon shade where summers are hot and humid. Avoid summer pruning and heavy fertilization, since flower buds form on the previous year's wood and lush new growth is more prone to disease.

common_name: Red Cloud Reflected in Snow Tree Peony (White Rockii Tree Peony with Red-Flushed Petal Bases)
scientific_name: Paeonia rockii 'Red Cloud Reflected in Snow'

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early to mid fall in deep, humus-rich, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun to partial afternoon shade, setting a grafted union (if present) 4-6 inches below the soil surface to encourage the scion to form its own roots.

directions: Red Cloud Reflected in Snow is a Paeonia rockii-type tree peony named for its snow-white petals washed with a cloud of red at the base of each bloom, a bold two-tone pattern typical of the finest rockii selections bred from wild Gansu mountain peony stock. This lineage tends toward superior cold hardiness compared with the more familiar Paeonia suffruticosa hybrids, tolerating harsh winters well into zone 4 once its root system is established. Grow in deep, humus-rich, sharply drained soil in a permanent site, with full sun in cooler regions and afternoon shade where summer heat is intense, since rockii tree peonies can decline in hot, humid conditions. Limit pruning to removing dead or damaged wood, since flowering wood is set the previous season.

common_name: Rose Petals Dusted with Gold Tree Peony (Pink Rockii Tree Peony with Golden Stamens)
scientific_name: Paeonia rockii 'Rose Petals Dusted with Gold'

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early to mid fall in deep, humus-rich, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun to partial afternoon shade, setting a grafted union (if present) 4-6 inches below the soil surface to encourage the scion to form its own roots.

directions: Rose Petals Dusted with Gold is a Paeonia rockii-type tree peony bearing large, rose-pink, semi-double to double flowers whose loosely arranged petals reveal a prominent central boss of golden-yellow stamens, giving the impression of gold dust scattered over the pink petals. As with other rockii-type tree peonies derived from wild mountain peony populations of Gansu Province, it tends to be more cold-hardy and tolerant of lean, sharply drained soils than the classic Paeonia suffruticosa hybrids. Plant in a permanent location in deep, fertile, well-drained soil, in full sun where summers are mild or afternoon shade where they are hot and humid. Avoid disturbing the root zone once established and limit pruning to dead or damaged wood, since flower buds form on the previous season's growth.

common_name: White Screen Reflects a Blue Jewel Tree Peony (White Rockii Tree Peony with Purple-Flared Center)
scientific_name: Paeonia rockii 'White Screen Reflects a Blue Jewel'

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early to mid fall in deep, humus-rich, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun to partial afternoon shade, setting a grafted union (if present) 4-6 inches below the soil surface to encourage the scion to form its own roots.

directions: White Screen Reflects a Blue Jewel is a Paeonia rockii-type tree peony displaying the group's signature banded pattern: broad white outer petals surrounding a jewel-like inner zone flushed with violet-blue at the base of each petal. This rockii lineage, derived from wild mountain peony populations native to Gansu Province in northwestern China, is prized for cold hardiness well beyond that of typical Paeonia suffruticosa hybrids and for tolerance of lean, rocky, sharply drained soils. Site the shrub permanently in deep, humus-rich soil in full sun where summers are mild, shifting to afternoon shade in hot-summer regions, since the flowers and foliage can scorch under intense heat. Prune only to remove dead or damaged wood after bloom, since next year's flowers are already set in the current season's stem buds.

common_name: Rosy Cheeks Tree Peony (Blush-Pink Rockii Tree Peony)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early to mid fall in deep, humus-rich, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun to partial afternoon shade, setting a grafted union (if present) 4-6 inches below the soil surface to encourage the scion to form its own roots.

directions: Rosy Cheeks is a Paeonia rockii-type tree peony bearing soft, blush-pink flowers deepening to a warmer rose tone toward the petal base, a gentler counterpart to the more strongly bicolor rockii selections. Bred from wild mountain peony stock native to Gansu Province, rockii-type tree peonies are generally more cold-hardy and better suited to lean, sharply drained soils than the widely sold Paeonia suffruticosa hybrids. Plant in a permanent site in deep, fertile, well-drained soil, giving full sun in cooler climates and afternoon shade where summer heat and humidity are intense. Once established, avoid transplanting and limit pruning to dead or damaged wood, since flower buds are produced on the previous year's growth.

common_name: Yan Chun Tree Peony (Rosy-Red Early-Season Rockii Tree Peony)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early to mid fall in deep, humus-rich, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun to partial afternoon shade, setting a grafted union (if present) 4-6 inches below the soil surface to encourage the scion to form its own roots.

directions: Yan Chun is a Paeonia rockii-type tree peony whose Chinese name translates loosely to "radiant spring," a nod to its warm rosy-red flowers that open among the earliest of the rockii tree peonies each season. Like other rockii-type selections, it traces to wild mountain peony populations of Gansu Province and tends toward greater cold hardiness and tolerance of lean, sharply drained soil than the more commonly sold Paeonia suffruticosa hybrids. Grow in a permanent site in deep, humus-rich soil in full sun where summers are mild, or afternoon shade where summers are hot and humid, since foliage and flower quality both suffer under intense heat stress. Prune only to remove dead or damaged wood, leaving the previous season's stems intact to carry the next year's flower buds.

common_name: Phoenix White Tree Peony (Single White Paeonia ostii Tree Peony)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early to mid fall in deep, humus-rich, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun to partial afternoon shade, setting a grafted union (if present) 4-6 inches below the soil surface to encourage the scion to form its own roots.

directions: Phoenix White (Feng Dan Bai in Chinese, referencing the mythical phoenix) is the classic selection of Paeonia ostii, a vigorous tree peony species native to central China long cultivated there both as an ornamental and as a seed-oil crop. It produces large, single to semi-double, pure white flowers with a prominent maroon-purple flare at the base of each petal and bright golden stamens, opening in great numbers on a taller, more upright, and notably faster-growing shrub than most Paeonia suffruticosa hybrids. Paeonia ostii tolerates a wider range of soils and climates than many tree peonies and is valued for its exceptional vigor, disease resistance, and reliable heavy bloom. Plant in deep, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade in a permanent location, and prune only to remove dead or damaged wood, since flowering wood is set the previous season.

common_name: Whitleyi Major Peony (Single White Heirloom Peony with Golden Stamens)

planting.note: Plant bare-root divisions in fall 4-6 weeks before the ground freezes, with eyes no more than 1-2 in below the soil surface, in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Whitleyi Major is an antique single-flowered Paeonia lactiflora cultivar, in commerce since the 1800s and long recognized with the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for its garden reliability. Each early-season bloom opens flat and saucer-shaped in pure white with a broad, showy central boss of golden-yellow stamens, a simpler and more naturalistic look than the fully double show peonies bred later, and one that reads especially well combined with old garden roses. Plant bare-root divisions in fall in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, setting the eyes no more than 1-2 inches below the soil surface, since deeper planting is the most common cause of peonies failing to flower. As a single-form cultivar its stems rarely need staking despite the size of the blooms, and established clumps can remain undisturbed and floriferous for decades.

common_name: Alba Plena Peony (Double White Heirloom Officinalis Peony)

planting.note: Plant bare-root divisions in fall 4-6 weeks before the ground freezes, with eyes no more than 1-2 in below the soil surface, in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Alba Plena is a fully double, creamy-white heirloom form of Paeonia officinalis documented in European gardens since at least the 16th century, the pale-flowered companion to the deep crimson 'Rubra Plena' with which it has long been paired in cottage garden borders. Like other officinalis cultivars it breaks dormancy and blooms earlier in spring than most Paeonia lactiflora cultivars, with dense, rounded, bomb-form flowers held over glossy, deeply cut foliage that remains ornamental well after bloom. Plant bare-root divisions in fall with the eyes only 1-2 inches below the soil surface in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, and avoid crowding by later-emerging perennials that could shade out its early growth. Established clumps resent division and disturbance, rewarding patient gardeners with reliable bloom for generations once settled.

planting.note: Plant bare-root divisions in fall 4-6 weeks before the ground freezes, with eyes no more than 1-2 in below the soil surface, in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Paeonia tenuifolia 'Plena' is the fully double form of the fernleaf peony, an extremely old cultivar known in European gardens since at least the 16th century and prized for combining the species' finely dissected, carrot-top-like foliage with dense, globular, deep blood-red double flowers. It blooms in mid-spring, earlier and on shorter stems than the Chinese hybrid garden peonies, and like the wild species it is a steppe plant that wants lean, sharply drained soil rather than the rich, moisture-retentive ground favored by Paeonia lactiflora. Plant bare-root divisions in fall, setting the eyes no more than 1-2 inches below the soil surface, in full sun in soil that drains quickly even in winter, since wet feet are the most common cause of failure. The ferny foliage remains an attractive fine-textured accent through summer even after the brief but showy bloom period ends.
